job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were playing in their garden in Bengaluru. Rohan pushed his toy car across the flat patio, and it rolled at a steady pace in a straight line. Meera watched it and said, 'It is moving at a constant speed because it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.' Later, they went to the park to watch a swing. Meera noticed that whether she pulled the swing back a little or a lot, the time taken for one complete back-and-forth movement remained the same. She explained, 'The time period of a pendulum does not depend on the amplitude of the swing.' Nearby, their father was jogging. He ran 2 kilometers in 20 minutes. Rohan calculated his father's speed by dividing the distance of 2 kilometers by the time of 1/3 of an hour, resulting in 6 kilometers per hour. He noted that even a slow-moving snail has a measurable speed. Finally, they looked at a distance-time graph in Rohan’s textbook. A horizontal line on the graph showed that the distance from the starting point did not change over time, meaning the object was at rest, not moving at all.

items.evidence: Meera watched it and said, 'It is moving at a constant speed because it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.'
items.q: How did Meera know the toy car was moving at a constant speed?
options: It covered the same distance in each equal time
It moved along a straight line on the patio
It travelled a long distance across the patio
It moved very fast across the flat patio
items.explain: Constant speed means equal distances are covered in equal intervals of time.

wrong.why: thinks moving in a straight line means uniform motion
thinks speed is the same as distance travelled
thinks only fast objects have a speed

items.evidence: She explained, 'The time period of a pendulum does not depend on the amplitude of the swing.'
items.q: Meera pulls the swing back much farther. What happens to the time for one full swing?
options: It stays the same as with a small pull
It gets longer because the swing travels farther
It gets shorter because the push is stronger
It doubles because it moves twice as far
items.explain: The time period of a pendulum does not depend on how far it is pulled back.

wrong.why: thinks a bigger amplitude increases the time period
thinks a stronger pull makes the swing faster
thinks time grows in proportion to swing distance

items.evidence: Rohan calculated his father's speed by dividing the distance of 2 kilometers by the time of 1/3 of an hour, resulting in 6 kilometers per hour.
items.q: Father ran 2 km in 20 minutes. Which working gives his speed in kilometers per hour?
items.explain: Speed is distance divided by time; 20 minutes is 1/3 hour, so 2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 km/h.

wrong.why: divides kilometers by minutes without converting
multiplies distance and time instead of dividing

items.evidence: A horizontal line on the graph showed that the distance from the starting point did not change over time, meaning the object was at rest, not moving at all.
items.q: A bus's distance-time graph shows a flat horizontal line. What is the bus doing?
options: It is standing still in one place
It is moving at a steady speed
It is moving along a flat road
It is moving very slowly, like a snail
items.explain: A horizontal line means distance does not change over time, so the bus is at rest.

wrong.why: thinks a horizontal line means constant speed
reads the graph's shape as the path's shape
picks the slow snail mentioned nearby in the passage
